correctness.rationale: Verified every essential inference in DRAFT.md Sec.2 from definitions. (1) Z0 finite: g<=1 on [-1,1], g<=|x|^-5 for |x|>=1 gives Z0<=2.5, >0 by positivity; sigma^2 finite: x^2 g(x)<=(1+x)^-3 integrable (integral 1/2), >0. So X=Y/sigma well-defined with E[X^2]=1; symmetry gives mean 0. (2) E[X^4]=inf: for x>=1, (1+x)^-5>=2^-5 x^-5 and L(x)^-1/2>=L(R)^-1/2 on [1,R], so int_1^R x^4 g >=2^-5 L(R)^-1/2 log R ~ sqrt(log R)->inf; scaling preserves infiniteness. (3) Two-sided Lee-Yin tail: upper T(t)<=c*/2 (1+t)^-4 L(t)^-1/2 via slowest-log pullout and exact int_t^inf (1+x)^-5=(1+t)^-4/4, giving limsup t^4T(log t)^{1/2}<=c*/2 using L(t)=log t+log(1+e/t). Lower lambda-block on [t,lambda t] gives T>=c*/2[(1+t)^-4-(1+lambda t)^-4]L(lambda t)^-1/2, so liminf>=c*/2(1-lambda^-4); lambda->inf after t->inf gives limit c*/2. Standardization P(|X|>s)=P(|Y|>sigma s) yields s^4P=(1+o(1))c'(log s)^-1/2 with c'=c*/(2 sigma^4)->0; log(sigma s)/log s->1 checked. (4) Obstruction: B_N=N^{1/2}(log N)^-2->inf, so p_N=(1+o(1))c'B_N^-4(log B_N)^-1/2; N^2B_N^-4=(log N)^8 and (log B_N)^-1/2=sqrt2(log N)^-1/2(1+o(1)) since log B_N=1/2 log N-2 loglog N, giving E(N)=(1+o(1))c'sqrt2(log N)^{15/2}->inf. With M=N(N-1)/2, P(no exceed)=(1-p_N)^M<=exp(-M p_N)->0 since M p_N~E(N)/2 and p_N->0. Threshold N^2B_N^-4(log B_N)^-1/2->0 is B_N>>N^{1/2}(log N)^-1/8 up to slowly varying factor; admitted -2 is strictly wrong side. TW1 limit explicitly attributed to Lee-Yin Thm 1.2 sufficiency (mean 0, variance 1, finite-variance diagonal, tail->0 all satisfied); no rate claimed, no new comparison claimed. Numerics labeled approximations, not relied on for limits. Scripts tail_moments.py and prove_squeeze.py rerun VERIFY_OK and agree (Z0~0.47704, sigma^2~0.28376, c'~13.02; E(N)/(log N)^{15/2} 37.6->19.3 approaching c'sqrt2~18.41). Proof is analytic; experimental evidence distinguished.
